auth.title: Grain API
highlights:
# Legacy Docs

If you were part of the API Beta you can find the legacy docs here:

- (V1) Personal API Docs
- (V1) Workspace API Docs

Please be aware that v1 will be sunset and some features won't be translated to v2. As such, we don't recommend usage of v1 anymore.

## Personal Access Token

These tokens can be generated to grant access to the API in a per-user basis. Requests authenticated with these tokens are considered as " Personal API" and will have the same level of access as the user that generated the token has.

PATs can be generated here: https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api

## Workspace Access Token

These tokens can be generated to grant access to the API for a general workspace use case.

Requests authenticated with these tokens are considered as "Workspace API" and will have access to ALL DATA from your workspace.

WAT's can be generated here, by users with access: https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api

## OAuth2 Flow

This authentication method is for developers building integrations with Grain to be used by any Grain users. Requests authenticated with these tokens are considered as " Personal API" and will have the same level of access as the authenticated user has.

The API supports a standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow, including the PKCE extension for client-side only authentication. A redirect URI prefix is required to register a new client. For browser-based client applications, a list of CORS origins can also be added.

### Diagram

```
sequenceDiagram
  participant you as You
  actor user as User
  participant grain as Grain
  
  Note right of you: Step 1
  you-->>grain: Request Client ID & Secret (manually)
  grain-->>you: Client ID & Secret

  Note right of you: Step 2
  user->>you: Requests OAuth
  you->>user: Open or Redirects to oauth2/authorize
  user->>grain: oauth2/authorize
  
  Note left of grain: Step 3
  grain->>user: Requests login
  user->>grain: Login
  
  grain->>user: Requests Confirm OAuth
  user->>grain: Confirms

	Note left of grain: Step 4  
  grain->>user: Redirects to redirect_uri w/code
  user->>you: redirect_uri w/code
  
  Note right of you: Step 5
  you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/code
  grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token
  
  Note right of you: Refresh
  you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/refresh_token
  grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token
```

### Step 1

Obtain the `client_id` and `client_secret` (only for server-side applications) credentials.

### Step 2

Open the url `https://grain.com/_/public-api/oauth2/authorize` with the following query params.

| Param |  |
| --- | --- |
| client_id | Obtained separately in Step 1 |
| redirect_uri | Must be prefixed by the registered URI prefix |
| response_type | Must be `code` |
| code_challenge | A random string, hashed with `SHA256` and `base64` URL encoded |
| code_challenge_method | Must be `S256` |

### Step 3

If the user is not already signed in to Grain, they will be prompted to sign in. After being authenticated, the user will be prompted to confirm the OAuth2 connection.

### Step 4

The user will be redirected to `redirect_uri` from Step 2 with the `code` query param.

### Step 5

Make a `POST` request to generate the token. See OAuth2 Generate Token

### Refresh Token

After the `access_token` has expired, you may generate a new one.

See OAuth2 Refresh Token

## Authenticating Calls

To authenticate API calls, the client must add the following header:

```jsx
Authorization: Bearer TOKEN
```

where `TOKEN` is either the access token obtained in the OAuth2 flow, a Personal Access Token or a Workspace Access Token.

# Versions

In addition to the authorization header, you must also include a `Public-Api-Version` header:

```jsx
Public-Api-Version: VERSION
```

Versions in the Grain-API will be used to introduce and/or deprecate fields.

Below is a list of supported versions:

| Versions |
| --- |
| 2025-10-31 * current version |

# Rate Limits

Grain allows a total of `300` requests per minute. Any requests beyond that limit will return a `429 Too Many Requests`

Additionally we also return the following headers with every request:

| Header |  |
| --- | --- |
| x-ratelimit-limit | Max number of requests allowed per window. (300/min) |
| x-ratelimit-remaining | Number of requests remaining in the current window. |
| Retry-After * only added if the request exceeded the limit | Number of seconds you must wait before submitting another request. |

# Endpoints

API Domain is: `https://api.grain.com`

### Generate Token

Endpoint

`POST /_/public-api/oauth2/token`

Params

| Param |  |
| --- | --- |
| client_id | Obtained separately in Step 1 |
| client_secret required for server-side applications | Obtained separately in Step 1 |
| grant_type | Must be `authorization_code` |
| code | String obtained in Step 4 |
| code_verifier | String sent as `code_challenge` in Step 2 |

Response

| Field |  |
| --- | --- |
| token_type | Always `bearer` |
| access_token | Token to be used in the `Authorization` header |
| refresh_token | Token to be used to refresh the access_token (See Refresh Token) |
| expires_in | Denotes how many seconds the access_token will live for after its generation. |

Note: Some legacy clients do not return `refresh_token` nor `expires_in`. For these cases the access_token does not expire.

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data '{"grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": "CODE", "client_id": "CLIENT_ID", "client_secret": "CLIENT_SECRET"}' \
     https://api.grain.com/_/public-api/oauth2/token
```

Example Response

```json
{
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "access_token": "aaaaa33333EEEEENNNNNoooooKKKKK33333lllll",
  "refresh_token": "IIIIIQQQQQxxxxx4444422222CCCCCoooooWWWWW",
  "expires_in": 3600
}
```

### Refresh Token

Endpoint

`POST /_/public-api/oauth2/token`

| Param |  |
| --- | --- |
| client_id | Obtained separately in Step 1 |
| client_secret required for server-side applications | Obtained separately in Step 1 |
| grant_type | Must be `refresh_token` |
| refresh_token | Obtained when generating or refreshing an access_token |

Response

| Field |  |
| --- | --- |
| token_type | Always `bearer` |
| access_token | Token to be used in the `Authorization` header |
| refresh_token | Token to be used to re-refresh the access_token |
| expires_in | Denotes how many seconds the access_token will live for after its generation. |

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data '{"grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": "IIIIIQQQQQxxxxx4444422222CCCCCoooooWWWWW", "client_id": "CLIENT_ID", "client_secret": "CLIENT_SECRET"}' \
     https://api.grain.com/_/public-api/oauth2/token
```

```json
{
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "access_token": "bbbbb44444FFFFFOOOOOpppppLLLLL44444mmmmm",
  "refresh_token": "JJJJJRRRRRyyyyy5555533333DDDDDpppppXXXXX",
  "expires_in": 3600
}
```

highlights:
# Authentication

Grain supports three authentication methods depending on your use case.

Personal Access Token (PAT): grants access on behalf of a single user. The token has the same permissions as the user who generated it. Best for personal automations or testing. Available on every plan, including Free. Click here to generate a PAT.

Workspace Access Token (WAT): grants access to all data in the workspace, regardless of which user owns it. Use this for server-side integrations where you need workspace-wide access. Requires admin access to generate and is available on Business and Enterprise plans. Click here to generate a WAT.

OAuth2: the standard flow for building integrations to be used by any Grain user. Users authorize your application directly, and your app receives a token scoped to that user's data. Required if you are building an integration to distribute to others.

...

# API version

The current API version is `2025-10-31`. All requests must include a `Public-Api-Version` header with this value. Grain uses versioning to introduce and deprecate fields without breaking existing integrations.

The v1 (beta) API was sunset in September 2026. Use v2 for all integrations. See the developer docs for migration details.

# FAQ

Do I need a specific Grain plan to use the API? Not for personal API access, which is available on every plan, including Free. Workspace API access is available on Business and Enterprise plans and requires admin access to generate.

Can I access recordings I did not attend? With a Personal Access Token, you can only access recordings within your own permission level. With a Workspace Access Token, you can access all recordings in the workspace.

...

Where do I generate my API token? Personal API tokens are generated in Account settings → Integrations → Personal API. They are available on every plan. Workspace API tokens are generated in Workspace settings → Integrations → API. Only workspace admins on Business and Enterprise plans can generate API tokens for the workspace.

Is there a sandbox environment for testing? No sandbox is available at this time. Test against your live workspace using a Personal Access Token scoped to your own account to limit exposure.

gate.title: Grain API | Grain
highlights:
# Grain API

Connect Grain to your own tools and workflows with the Grain public API.

Table of contents

The Grain API lets developers read meeting data, manage recordings, and receive real-time events from Grain programmatically. Use it to build custom integrations, sync data to internal systems, or automate workflows that go beyond what Grain's built-in integrations support.

For the full technical reference, see developers.grain.com.

# What you can do with the API

Read meeting data: retrieve recordings, transcripts, AI notes and action items, participants, tags, teams, and meeting types from your workspace.

Manage recordings: upload external recordings to Grain, update recording metadata, add or remove tags, and control sharing at the user or team level.

Download recordings: export video files and transcripts in multiple formats (JSON, plain text, VTT, SRT) for archiving or processing.

Receive real-time events: register webhooks to receive a payload whenever a new recording is processed in your workspace, so downstream systems stay in sync without polling.

# Authentication

Grain supports three authentication methods depending on your use case.

Personal Access Token (PAT): grants access on behalf of a single user. The token has the same permissions as the user who generated it. Best for personal automations or testing. Available on every plan, including Free. Click here to generate a PAT.

Workspace Access Token (WAT): grants access to all data in the workspace, regardless of which user owns it. Use this for server-side integrations where you need workspace-wide access. Requires admin access to generate and is available on Business and Enterprise plans. Click here to generate a WAT.

OAuth2: the standard flow for building integrations to be used by any Grain user. Users authorize your application directly, and your app receives a token scoped to that user's data. Required if you are building an integration to distribute to others.

# Rate limits

The API allows 300 requests per minute per token. Requests beyond this limit return a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Each response includes rate limit headers so you can track remaining capacity.

...

# API version

The current API version is `2025-10-31`. All requests must include a `Public-Api-Version` header with this value. Grain uses versioning to introduce and deprecate fields without breaking existing integrations.

The v1 (beta) API was sunset in September 2026. Use v2 for all integrations. See the developer docs for migration details.

# FAQ

Do I need a specific Grain plan to use the API? Not for personal API access, which is available on every plan, including Free. Workspace API access is available on Business and Enterprise plans and requires admin access to generate.

Can I access recordings I did not attend? With a Personal Access Token, you can only access recordings within your own permission level. With a Workspace Access Token, you can access all recordings in the workspace.

Can I upload recordings from other platforms into Grain? Yes. The API supports uploading external recordings, which Grain will then transcribe and process as if they were captured natively.

Where do I generate my API token? Personal API tokens are generated in Account settings → Integrations → Personal API. They are available on every plan. Workspace API tokens are generated in Workspace settings → Integrations → API. Only workspace admins on Business and Enterprise plans can generate API tokens for the workspace.

Is there a sandbox environment for testing? No sandbox is available at this time. Test against your live workspace using a Personal Access Token scoped to your own account to limit exposure.

gate.title: Plans | Grain
highlights:
# Plans

Compare Grain's Free, Pro, Business and Enterprise plans.

 Updated over a week ago

Table of contents

For current pricing, see grain.com/pricing.

# Free: $0

For individuals getting started. Free is for one person, so there's no shared workspace.

# Pro: $15 per month billed yearly, or $19 monthly

For individuals who've outgrown Free. Pro is also for one person.

- Unlimited meetings, up to 4 hours each
- Unlimited meeting history
- Unlimited uploads and imports, each under 3 hours
- Custom AI prompts and note templates, custom vocabulary
- No watermark

# Business: $29 per seat per month billed yearly, or $39 monthly

For companies sharing meeting memory and AI. Minimum 2 seats.

- Shared company workspace with admin controls, teams, and team libraries with custom recording and sharing rules
- Free Lite seats: invite teammates to watch, comment and clip
- Unlimited meetings up to 8 hours each; unlimited uploads, each under 3 hours
- Slack, HubSpot, Salesforce and Aircall, including CRM field autofill
- Conversation intelligence: AI coaching, trackers and talk-time metrics
- Custom AI follow-up emails
- Advanced MCP for Claude and ChatGPT; workspace API and webhooks. Learn more about Grain's MCP here.
- Recording consent, sensitive meeting detection and data retention policies
- Free data migration from other AI notetakers

# Enterprise

Everything in Business, plus SAML SSO and SCIM, audit logs, 1080p recording, bring your own LLM (Azure, Bedrock, Vertex), custom data retention, custom invoicing and payment terms, priority support with an SLA, and a dedicated account manager.

Contact sales@grain.com or book a demo.

# Choosing a plan

- Just you: start on Free; move to Pro for longer meetings, full history and unlimited uploads.
- A team that wants to share meetings in one place: Business.
- Strict security needs (SSO, SCIM, audit logs): Enterprise.

# FAQ

Can my team use Free or Pro together? Free and Pro are for one person. Each person can have their own account, but there's no shared workspace, so you can't see each other's meetings in one place. You can still share a single recording by link. For a shared workspace, choose Business.

Can I mix plans in one workspace? No. All Full seats in a workspace are on the same plan.

Is there a free trial? Yes. If you're a workspace admin on Free and signed up with a company email address, you can start a 14-day Grain Business trial yourself, with no credit card. Each workspace can start one trial, and it moves back to Free at the end unless you upgrade. If you can't start one yourself, click 'Request a trial' on the plans page and we'll set it up for you.

My company already uses Grain. If your company's email domain already has a Grain workspace you can join, join it rather than starting a new Business workspace.

How do annual and monthly billing differ? Annual billing is charged upfront at a lower per-seat price. Monthly billing is charged each month at a higher price.

## Overview

Add Grain to any ModuleX agent or workflow. Access Grain meeting recordings, transcripts, highlights, and AI-generated summaries through the Grain public REST API (`api.grain.com/_/public-api`). List and retrieve recordings, fetch full transcripts, browse teams, meeting types, and views, and manage webhook subscriptions for recording events.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> Categories: Productivity & Collaboration · Meeting · Note Taking · Auth: API Key · Actions: 9

## Authentication

### API Key Authentication

Authenticate using your Grain personal access token

1. Step 1

Log in to your Grain account at https://grain.com

2. Step 2

Open Settings and navigate to the API / Integrations section

3. Step 3

Create a Personal Access Token (developer access may require approval)

4. Step 4

Paste the access token below

#### Required Credentials

| Field | Description | Required | Format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Grain API Key | Your Grain personal access token | Yes | `-` |

...

## Limits & Quotas

- The Grain public API requires the `Public-Api-Version` header
(currently `2025-10-31`) on the recording, transcript, team, and
meeting-type endpoints.
- Developer access to the public API is in beta and may be limited to
approved partners.
- Error model: non-2xx responses and timeouts are caught and
returned as `success=False` + `error` rather than raising. Plan for
retries on the agent side based on the error string.

mcp.title: Grain MCP | Grain
highlights:
# Grain MCP

Connect Grain to Claude or ChatGPT and query your meeting data with natural language.

 Updated this week

Table of contents

Grain's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server gives AI assistants direct access to your meetings, transcripts, AI notes, and workspace data. Ask questions, generate reports, create clips, and organize recordings, all from your AI chat interface.

For technical setup and the full tool reference, see the Grain MCP developer docs.

# Set up with Claude

Step 1: Add the Claude Connector integration

1. In Claude, go to ’Customize’ → ‘Connectors’
2. Click '+' to search for connectors
3. Search for ‘Grain’
4. Select & connect Grain
5. You’ll be redirected to Grain to approve the connection

Step 2: Verify

From a new Claude chat, send this test prompt:

```
Tell me about my most recent Grain meeting
```

If the MCP doesn’t work as expected, click '+' and confirm 'Grain' appears under 'Connectors' before trying again.

# Set up with ChatGPT

Step 1: Add the ChatGPT App integration

1. Go to 'Apps' and search for 'Grain'
2. Select 'Grain' and click 'Connect'
3. Sign in and approve ChatGPT access to your Grain account data

Step 2: Verify

From a new ChatGPT chat, send the following test prompt:

```
Tell me about my most recent Grain meeting
```

If the MCP doesn’t work properly, click '+' and select Grain as a source before trying again.

# Set up with Cursor

Click the link below to install with a single command:

Set up Grain in Cursor →

# All plans

- Search meetings by company, person, date range, or topic
- Get transcripts and AI-generated notes for any meeting
- Retrieve action items from a meeting
- Access your private notes on a recording
- Create clips from any meeting
- Tag meetings to organize your workspace
- Create and manage playlists and stories

# Business & Enterprise plans

- Get AI-generated sales coaching insights and scorecards
- Access deal intelligence via HubSpot integration
- Get Grain's Company Memory for context about the companies you work with across all your meetings
- Share or unshare meetings with your teams or the whole workspace

For the full tool list and parameters, see Available MCP Tools.

# Example prompts

Meeting research

- "Show me all action items I'm responsible for from the past 7 days."
- "Who from Acme Corp have we met with and what topics did we cover?"
- "What objections came up in external sales calls this week?"

Content creation

- "Clip the section where the client talks about their timeline."
- "Tag all meetings from last week with external participants as #client-calls."
- "Create a playlist called 'Onboarding Best Practices' and add my last five training calls."

# Pre-built reports

Grain provides structured report prompts accessible in Claude via ’+’ → ‘Connectors’ → ‘Add from Grain’. These chain multiple steps into full reports.

...

# FAQ

Is my data safe? Grain's MCP server uses OAuth and HTTPS. Developers can also connect with a personal access token; see the developer docs. Your data stays in your Grain account and is processed temporarily by AI to answer your questions. View your connected AI client's privacy policy for more information about data handling.

What data can the MCP access? Only data you already have access to in Grain — meetings you attended, contacts, AI notes, transcripts, and deal info (with HubSpot connected). It cannot access meetings you weren't part of.

Can I control which capabilities my AI client uses? Yes. In Claude’s ‘Connectors’ menu you can toggle individual Grain tools on or off. ChatGPT offers a similar feature, allowing you to specify when ChatGPT should ask for permission to use an MCP tool.

mcp.title: Official Grain MCP Server | Grain
highlights:
# Official Grain MCP Server

Announced: June 18, 2025

Mike Adams

Grain's official MCP server is available now for all users! 🎉

With Grain's new MCP server you can securely access your meetings, notes, transcripts, deals, & coaching scorecard data natively using Anthropic's new Claude Integrations (ChatGPT coming soon), or using `mcp-remote` in Cursor, Windsurf and other clients.

In addition to being able to ask any prompt in Cluade with Grain data, the server includes built-in MCP Prompts to run one-click reports like:

- 📣 Weekly "Voice of the Customer" reports to track sentiment & requests
- 📊 Pipeline IQ analysis to identify high opportunity & at-risk deals

# Grain `Grain` connects an agent to Grain's hosted MCP server. The agent can search and read the meetings, transcripts, notes, and deals the signed-in user can see, and create clips and tag meetings unless you set `read_only=True`. Source > While Pydantic AI Harness is on 0.x releases, the API may change between minor releases; when it does, deprecation warnings and release-note migration guidance tell you (or your agent) exactly how to upgrade. See the version policy. ```mermaid flowchart TB accTitle: Grain: meetings, transcripts and notes through Grain's MCP server accDescr: Your agent's model calls tools prefixed grain_ and gets results. The Grain capability gets a token for each run from your auth function, sends tools/call with an OAuth Bearer token to the Grain MCP server at api.grain.com/_/mcp, and with read_only=True drops tools not marked read-only. As the run starts, the server rejects an invalid or expired token with 401 and the run raises. subgraph agent["Your agent"] model(["model"]) auth["auth function"] grain["Grain()
grain_"]:::capability end dropped["tools not marked
read-only, with
read_only=True"]:::blocked server["Grain MCP server
api.grain.com/_/mcp"]:::external expired["invalid or expired token:
401, the run raises"]:::blocked model <-->|"tool call, result"| grain auth -->|"token for each run"| grain grain <-->|"tools/call,
OAuth Bearer token"| server grain -.-x|"drops"| dropped ... classDef capability stroke:#E520E9,stroke-width:2px classDef external stroke:#0E9C86,stroke-width:2px classDef blocked stroke:#E5533D,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:4 3 ``` ## Before you start Grain MCP works on every Grain plan. The deal and coaching tools need the Business or Enterprise plan. Grain MCP takes an OAuth access token, which Grain issues only through the standard MCP authorization flow. The server supports dynamic client registration, so any MCP OAuth client library can sign the user in. Pass the token it returns as `auth` or `GRAIN_ACCESS_TOKEN`. ... ## Connect ```python from pydantic_ai import Agent from pydantic_ai_harness import Grain agent = Agent('openai:gpt-6.1-sol', capabilities=[Grain()]) result = agent.run_sync('Summarize my most recent Grain meeting') print(result.output) ``` Set `GRAIN_ACCESS_TOKEN` to a Grain access token, or pass `auth=` a token. On your own machine, `auth='oauth'` signs you in through the browser instead. To serve several users from one agent, pass a function instead (see Per-user credentials). ## Per-user credentials `auth` decides which Grain account each run uses: `auth` Account used Not set, `None`, or `''` `GRAIN_ACCESS_TOKEN`. If that is not set either, creating the agent raises an error. An access token That token, for every run. `'oauth'` The account you sign in to through the browser. This only works on your own machine. A function Called at the start of each run, and can be async. The token it returns is used for that run. If it returns `None` or `''`, that run has no Grain tools. A function never uses `GRAIN_ACCESS_TOKEN`, and must not return `'oauth'`. A fixed token or `GRAIN_ACCESS_TOKEN` suits a script or an agent on your own machine, where every run is the same account. ... Grain connects when the run starts, even with `defer_loading=True`. If the token is invalid or expired, the run raises an `httpx.HTTPStatusError` with status 401, so return `None` from the function when you know the token is no longer valid. ... ## Tool names The agent sees each of the server's tools under the `grain_` prefix, as in `grain_`, so they don't collide with other tools on the agent. Set `tool_prefix` to use a different prefix, or `tool_prefix=None` to keep the names the server gives them. `read_only` selects tools by what the server marks as read-only, not by name, so the prefix does not change what it keeps. A toolset wrapper on `capability.get_toolset()`, such as `filtered()`, sees the names the agent sees, prefix included. ... ## Tool selection and approval `read_only=True` gives the agent only the tools that Grain's server labels as read-only, and leaves out all the others. If Grain has not labeled its read tools, the agent gets no Grain tools and emits an `MCPReadOnlyNoToolsWarning`. The token's permissions still decide what the agent can reach. Transcripts and meeting titles contain text from everyone in the meeting, including external guests, and that text reaches the model as tool output. Use `read_only=True` or require approval if the agent should not change Grain data. `include_instructions=False` stops the server's own instructions from reaching the agent. To filter tools or require approval in your application, wrap the toolset with the existing toolset wrappers. For example, this asks for approval before every tool call, so you decide which meeting data reaches the model: ```python from pydantic_ai import Agent from pydantic_ai.messages import DeferredToolRequests from pydantic_ai_harness import Grain capability = Grain() agent = Agent( 'openai:gpt-6.1-sol', toolsets=[capability.get_toolset().approval_required()], output_type=[str, DeferredToolRequests], ) ``` Handle the approval requests with the deferred tools workflow. To cap the size of tool output, add Tool Output Limits. ## Connection customization Pass `client` (a FastMCP client or transport) to control the connection yourself, for example to add a proxy or MCP handlers. The client owns the URL and authentication, so it cannot be combined with `auth`. `read_only` and `include_instructions` still apply. A `client` is one connection shared by every run; see Per-user credentials to connect each user separately.

## About Grain MCP Server

Grain turns meetings into insights, summaries, and next steps. Its connector brings meeting context into assistant workflows so users can find moments, understand decisions, and convert conversations into follow-up actions.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the Grain remote MCP server?

The Grain remote MCP server is a hosted Model Context Protocol endpoint at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp, so AI assistants can connect to it without installing or running anything locally.

### How do I connect to the Grain MCP server?

Add the endpoint https://api.grain.com/_/mcp to any MCP-compatible client such as Claude Code, Cursor, or VS Code. The setup snippets on this page configure each client in one step.

### Does the Grain MCP server require authentication?

Yes. Grain uses OAuth: the first time you connect, your MCP client opens a browser window to sign in and authorize access, then reuses the credentials for future sessions.

### Which transport does the Grain MCP server use?

Grain exposes a Streamable HTTP endpoint, the transport used by remote MCP servers and supported by all major MCP clients.
